rationale:
`requirements.sdk.validation-cache.intern_node` has three obligations. Equal data yields the same handle, distinct data yields distinct handles, and equal data yields one handle even when interned concurrently. The tests cover each one.

- **Concurrent equal data.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[clones_interning_the_same_data_concurrently_get_one_handle]` starts 4 threads behind a `Barrier`. Each thread interns `Node(42)` through a clone of the cache. The test asserts that all 4 returned ids equal `ids[0]`. It also asserts that `node_data` returns `Node(42)` for that id.
- **Distinct data.** The same test asserts `assert_ne!(cache.intern_node(Node(43)), ids[0])`. A cache that returned one handle for everything would fail this.
- **Sequential equal data across clones.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[saved_node_and_edge_inputs_survive_a_different_handle_allocation_order]` interns `Node(2)` and then `Node(1)`. It asserts that interning `Node(1)` again through `first.clone().cache()` returns the same handle as the review's `subject`. This covers the sequential "equal data gives the same handle" case. It also shows that the cache is shared across clones.

Both tests carry `{test}` references to `intern_node`, so there is no marking gap.

The distinct-data check compares only one pair of values. The requirement draws no further distinction among inputs, so I don't count that as a gap.

text: `intern_node` returns a handle for the supplied node data. Equal data always yields the same handle in this cache, including concurrent calls. Distinct data yields distinct handles.
pub fn intern_node(&self, data: D::NodeData) -> NodeId<D>;
